title: When the order of bird calls matters
review_depth: Primary-paper methods, results and figure captions reviewed via author-uploaded text; interpretive commentary also consulted. No replication.
finding: Japanese tit playback experiments link call combinations and order to distinct receiver responses.
limitations: This supports a bounded interpretation in this species. Commentary distinguishes compositionality from stronger human-like systematicity; general language ability is not established.
lesson: Test a proposed meaning against receiver behavior and carefully matched controls.
next_review: Ask a qualified researcher which inference and controls could transfer to the chosen pilot.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
study_snapshot: Study unit
21 birds in the first playback experiment; 34 in the ordering experiment.
Design
First experiment: within-bird call components, combined calls and background control, with randomized treatment order.
Ordering test
17 birds per condition: natural versus reversed sequences, with other acoustic features matched.
Outcomes
Scanning and speaker approach, rather than an AI-generated verbal interpretation.
review_locator: Suzuki et al.: Methods, Experiments 1–2; Figures 3–4. Phillips & Wilson: opening argument on systematicity.

title: Patterns inside sperm whale codas
review_depth: Primary study summary in founding audit; full-text methods review pending.
finding: Analysis of sperm whale codas describes contextual and combinatorial acoustic structure.
limitations: Conversational context and structural variation are not an English vocabulary or evidence of unrestricted translation.
lesson: Model temporal structure while keeping claims about meaning separate from claims about acoustic patterns.
next_review: Review the segmentation, individual identities and contextual definitions before reproducing a result.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: A birth, a group, and changing vocal styles
review_depth: Primary study summary in founding audit; full-text methods review pending.
finding: A reported sperm whale birth connects changing vocal styles with an observed social event.
limitations: A single event offers a valuable observation, but cannot establish a general call dictionary or causal interpretation.
lesson: Attach synchronized behavioral context to sound, and retain the event as the unit of analysis.
next_review: Identify which interpretations could be tested in independent events.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: NatureLM-audio: a useful starting point
review_depth: Official model card and project documentation; Hugging Face revision 77855d9b0acd039f90798dcf0861f626bfefbd6f recorded. No inference run.
finding: NatureLM-audio provides a foundation-model approach to describing and classifying biological sounds.
limitations: Descriptions are predictions, not verified animal intentions. The reviewed model lists CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; parent-model terms also matter. A paid deployment has not been cleared.
lesson: Inspect a frozen release, its training data and license before using it in an evaluation or paid product.
next_review: Compare a permitted model against a simple baseline on independently labeled recordings.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: BirdNET: identification before interpretation
review_depth: Official repository and license/review documentation reviewed for the audit.
finding: BirdNET supplies bird-sound identification tools and a human review workflow for detections.
limitations: Identification does not establish meaning. Main package code is MIT and listed models are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; separate STM32 artifacts use Apache-2.0. Check the exact release.
lesson: Reuse existing identification and review capabilities where they fit instead of assuming a new platform is necessary.
next_review: Choose an exact artifact, inspect its terms, and measure errors on the intended recordings.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Perch: reusable representations of animal sound
review_depth: Official model card, repository migration notice, Hoplite README and frozen model configuration reviewed; no inference run.
finding: Perch supplies acoustic embeddings for downstream classifiers. The current practical tooling route is Perch-Hoplite.
limitations: Listed model terms are Apache-2.0, but task performance, training-data overlap and the exact downloaded bundle remain unverified. CPU and GPU variants differ.
lesson: Consider a frozen embedding baseline once the species, labels and data rights are established.
next_review: Verify the CPU artifact, preprocessing and runtime on permitted recordings before selecting it for an experiment.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: DolphinGemma and shared signals
review_depth: Official announcement reviewed; not an independent replication.
finding: DolphinGemma models patterns in dolphin sounds. The related CHAT work uses learned shared signals in human-dolphin interactions.
limitations: Learning a shared interface and translating spontaneous natural communication are distinct scientific tasks.
lesson: Choose which question a pilot is trying to answer before selecting the interface or model.
next_review: Keep natural-call interpretation and taught-symbol experiments in separate protocols.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: What bark classification can tell us
review_depth: Published paper sections 3–6 reviewed; Tables 3–5 visually checked. No code execution or replication.
finding: Human-speech-pretrained Wav2Vec2 improved performance on selected dog-vocalization classification tasks.
limitations: Grounding uses four selected, stranger-related categories mixing vocal form and context. These results do not establish broad emotional or language translation.
lesson: Grouped evaluation is existing practice. Define independent behavioral labels and a stronger task-specific baseline.
next_review: Verify data access and exact model terms before proposing a replication.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
study_snapshot: Dataset
74 dogs; 16,789 segments across 14 labels, including non-dog sounds.
Evaluation
Ten-fold dog-grouped evaluation for context, breed and sex; identity recognition uses a different split.
Context result
62.18% accuracy versus 56.37% majority baseline: +5.81 percentage points.
Availability
Paper offers dataset and baselines by request; redistribution permission is not established.
review_locator: Published pages 16481–16484: Dataset, Experimental Setup, Grounding, Table 4 and Limitations.

title: Giving parrots a choice to connect
review_depth: Published PDF pages 4–10 and limitations reviewed; Table 2–4 layout checked. No independent reanalysis.
finding: Nine parrots used a caregiver-assisted video-call interface; the study reports greater engagement during the live phase.
limitations: Live always preceded playback. Reciprocity, caregiver cues and variable devices also complicate interpretation. Engagement is not a direct welfare or language measure.
lesson: Preserve the animal’s ability to stop, separate caregiver impressions from behavior, and account for condition order.
next_review: Review design and table-level inconsistencies with a specialist before adopting quantitative claims.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
study_snapshot: Study unit
Nine home-kept parrots over six months.
Design
Six live sessions followed by six playback sessions; conditions were not counterbalanced.
Measures
Call initiation, engagement duration and caregiver interviews/questionnaires.
Support
Behavior-specialist training, ongoing review and stopping provisions formed part of the study.
review_locator: CHI 2024 published version: sections 3–7, pages 4–11; Tables 2–4 on page 9.

title: Learned buttons and receiver responses
review_depth: University study report and vendor description reviewed; primary paper review pending.
finding: Research-team reporting describes appropriate responses by trained dogs to selected soundboard words.
limitations: This is evidence about responses to learned cues, not unrestricted conversation or a natural canine-language translation.
lesson: A learned shared interface needs different evaluation from an acoustic classifier.
next_review: Review cue controls and distinguish comprehension evidence from spontaneous production claims.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Plants emit signals we can measure
review_depth: Indexed primary-paper abstract reviewed; full-text methods review pending.
finding: The reported experiments describe airborne sounds from plants under stress and informative differences in recordings.
limitations: Informative emissions do not, by themselves, establish intentional communication or human-like language.
lesson: Measure a biological signal without converting a model-generated narrative into a scientific claim.
next_review: Review instrumentation and environmental controls before treating a sound as plant-derived.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: When another organism responds
review_depth: Primary-source summary and university account reviewed; full-text methods review pending.
finding: Research reports that female moths incorporate plant acoustic emissions into oviposition decisions.
limitations: The finding concerns a bounded plant-animal interaction. It does not establish conversation with trees.
lesson: Receiver behavior is a stronger test of biological relevance than signal classification alone.
next_review: Review playback controls, species and experimental conditions; do not generalize to all plants or insects.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Fungal electricity needs careful controls
review_depth: Methods discussion and critique reviewed for the audit; no independent replication performed.
finding: Measurement work and critiques highlight difficulties in separating fungal electrical activity from environmental artifacts.
limitations: A detected pattern or analogy to words is not evidence of a semantic language.
lesson: Instrumentation and controls must come before language claims or a translation interface.
next_review: Keep fungi in the reading program until a qualified collaborator defines a feasible measurement question.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: Start with tools researchers already use
review_depth: Official tool documentation reviewed for the audit.
finding: Arbimon, BORIS and BirdNET review tools already cover parts of acoustic analysis, behavioral annotation and detection review.
limitations: Feature availability does not prove an unmet product need or interchangeability between annotation formats.
lesson: Interview researchers using real workflows. An upstream contribution may be more useful than another platform.
next_review: Attempt one end-to-end annotation/export task and document a concrete gap before building an integration.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: A benchmark is only as useful as its labels
review_depth: BEANS task configuration and BEANS-Next card, displayed metadata and license description reviewed. No full data audit or experiment.
finding: Public benchmarks cover different tasks: the BEANS dog labels identify individuals, while BEANS-Next includes acoustic-description tasks.
limitations: These labels do not automatically provide observed behavior or intended meaning. BEANS-Next lists noncommercial terms and source-specific licenses. Training overlap is unresolved.
lesson: Select the scientific question first, then verify that the dataset measures it and supports an independent evaluation.
next_review: Inspect a relevant component, original annotations, group structure and rights after choosing the pilot question.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.

title: A usable parrot dataset starts with its labels
review_depth: Primary abstract/introduction and official repository documentation reviewed; selected scripts and the 2020 annotation CSV inspected. Full statistical methods, supplemental methods and audio not reviewed.
finding: The study reports vocal individuality in monk parakeets. Its public repository provides code, bird identifiers and behavioral notes. Our metadata sample has 808 annotation rows; 752 contain behavior text.
limitations: Rows are not necessarily individual calls. The 176 distinct nonempty behavior strings mix visible actions, vocal events and interpretations. Missing identities, uncertainty and audio/session linkage require review. Caller identity is not translation.
lesson: Keep source recordings, independent behavior labels and subject/session groups linked. Audit labels before selecting a model.
next_review: Inspect selection-table joins, normalize only observable behaviors, assess annotation reliability and evaluate whether enough independent groups remain.
expert_review: Not yet independently reviewed by a scientific specialist.
